title: Emergencies, nets and message handling
blurb: Know which rules apply in emergencies, how ARES and RACES differ, how nets run, and how formal messages are structured.

T2C01.why: **FCC rules always apply**, whether you're in ARES, RACES or following a FEMA plan.

T2C02.why: The NCS **calls the net to order and directs stations** checking in. It doesn't set the schedule or check licenses.

T2C03.why: Spell unusual words with the **standard phonetic alphabet**.
T2C03.trap: Q-codes and Morse aren't the standard way to clarify voice words.

T2C04.why: **RACES** is an FCC Part 97 amateur service for **civil defense communications** in national emergencies.
T2C04.trap: It isn't tied to CB, and a sprint is a contest.

T2C05.why: In a net, **traffic** means **formal messages** exchanged by net stations.
T2C05.trap: It's not the count of check-ins.

T2C06.why: **ARES** is licensed amateurs who volunteer and register their qualifications and equipment for public-service communications.
T2C06.trap: It isn't a military group or a licensing course.

T2C07.why: Unless you have an emergency, **transmit only when directed by net control**.
T2C07.trap: No home address, per-transmission time logging or FCC-database details are needed.

T2C08.why: **Winlink** relays messages using email addresses based on call signs.
T2C08.trap: FT8, PSK31 and AMTOR are digital modes, not email systems.

T2C09.why: Only when **immediate safety of human life or protection of property** is involved.
T2C09.trap: Not even a FEMA or RACES plan alone grants extra privileges.

T2C10.why: A message's **preamble** carries the information needed to **track** it.
T2C10.trap: Recipient contact details belong to the address.

T2C11.why: In a radiogram header, **check** is the **word count of the text**, so receivers can verify it.
T2C11.trap: It isn't a tick box or relay list.

T2C12.why: **RACES** requires certification by a civil defense agency.
